hints.tooltip: Optional hints/keywords (names, terms) to improve recognition.

output_format.tooltip: File save format only (does not change subtitle output).

output_path.tooltip: Optional output file path (relative goes to ComfyUI output).

split_mode.tooltip: Sentence splitting strategy. 'split_by_punctuation_or_pause' is recommended for natural, readable subtitle clauses without arbitrary character slicing.

max_gap_sec.tooltip: Max silence gap to keep the same sentence.

max_chars.tooltip: Optional max characters per line (0 = no limit, 80 recommended if length splitting is enabled).

max_inference_batch_size.tooltip: Batch size for inference/alignment to avoid OOM.

normalize_text.tooltip: Normalize spoken numbers ('一百二十八' -> '128') and acronym spacing ('A S R' -> 'ASR').

ApplyTextureToMesh.name: ApplyTextureToMesh
ApplyTextureToMesh.description: Attaches baked texture IMAGEs to a mesh's UV layout for SaveGLB. Feed the SAME mesh you baked

volume.tooltip: Volume adjustment in decibels (dB). 0 = no change, +6 = double, -6 = half, etc

AudioAdjustVolume.name: AudioAdjustVolume
AudioAdjustVolume.description: Adjust the volume of the audio by a specified amount in decibels (dB).

direction.tooltip: Whether to append audio2 after or before audio1.

AudioConcat.name: AudioConcat
AudioConcat.description: Concatenates the audio1 to audio2 in the specified direction.

merge_method.tooltip: The method used to combine the audio waveforms.

AudioMerge.name: AudioMerge
AudioMerge.description: Combine two audio tracks by overlaying their waveforms.

samples.tooltip: Rays per texel. More = smoother, slower. Raise if grainy.

max_distance.tooltip: Ray length, as a fraction of the bounding box diagonal. Smaller = tighter, more local occlusion.

bias.tooltip: Ray origin lift off the surface, as a fraction of the bounding box diagonal. Raise if even surfaces show dark blotches/holes.

BakeAmbientOcclusion.name: BakeAmbientOcclusion
BakeAmbientOcclusion.description: Bakes an ambient-occlusion map from a high-poly mesh into a low-poly's UV layout (white = open, dark = crevices). Feed the UV-unwrapped low_poly and the high_poly it was decimated from. Outputs a grayscale image for Apply Texture To Mesh's occlusion input (packed into the ORM map / occlusionTexture).

cage_distance.tooltip: Surface search band, as a fraction of the bounding box diagonal. Raise for wrong/missing patches under heavy decimation; lower if it grabs across gaps.

ignore_backfaces.tooltip: Skip high-poly surfaces facing away from the texel, so crevices/enclosed spaces don't grab the opposite wall. Disable only if the high-poly winding is inconsistent.

BakeNormalMapFromMesh.name: BakeNormalMapFromMesh
BakeNormalMapFromMesh.description: Bakes a tangent-space normal map (glTF/OpenGL +Y) from a high-poly mesh into a low-poly's UV layout, capturing detail lost during decimation. Feed the UV-unwrapped low_poly and the high_poly it was decimated from. Outputs an image for Apply Texture To Mesh's normal_map input.

reference_mesh.tooltip: Optional dense pre-decimation mesh; back-projects each texel onto its true surface before sampling, removing faceted baking on coarse meshes.

BakeTextureFromVoxel.name: BakeTextureFromVoxel
BakeTextureFromVoxel.description: Bakes PBR textures onto the mesh's existing UV layout (trilinear-sample the sparse voxel volume). Does NOT unwrap — connect a UV unwrap node upstream. Outputs base_color + metallic/roughness grayscale IMAGEs (black if no PBR); feed them to ApplyTextureToMesh (SAME mesh) for SaveGLB.

source_video.tooltip: Source video to edit or restyle (v2v, rv2v). Resized to width/height and trimmed to length.

reference_video.tooltip: Video to insert into the source video (ads2v).

reference_image.tooltip: Reference image injected as an in-context token (r2v, rv2v).

ref_max_size.tooltip: Max size for the long edge of reference_video and reference_images. Resized with preserved aspect ratio and snapped to 16px.

BerniniConditioning.name: BerniniConditioning
BerniniConditioning.description: Conditioning node for Bernini in-context video/image conditioning. It can be used for the following tasks: t2v (text-to-video), v2v (video-to-video), rv2v (reference-guided video editing), r2v (reference-to-video), ads2v (insert image/video into video).Reference images injected as in-context tokens (r2v, rv2v) are encoded independently at their own native aspect ratio (long edge capped at ref_max_size)

pre_cfg.tooltip: If true, rescale the combined noise BEFORE the sampler's CFG combine, without clamping (can amplify). Matches the norm-scaled CFG used by models like Lens. Default false keeps the original post-CFG x0-space attenuate-only behavior.

CFGOverride.name: CFGOverride
CFGOverride.description: Override cfg to a fixed value over a [start, end] percent (sigma) range. With multiple overrides, the one nearest the sampler wins on overlap.

clip.tooltip: The CLIP model used for encoding the text.

CLIPTextEncode.name: CLIPTextEncode
CLIPTextEncode.description: Encodes a text prompt using a CLIP model into an embedding that can be used to guide the diffusion model towards generating specific images.
output_tooltips: A conditioning containing the embedded text used to guide the diffusion model.

ckpt_name.tooltip: The name of the checkpoint (model) to load.

CheckpointLoaderSimple.name: CheckpointLoaderSimple
CheckpointLoaderSimple.description: Loads a diffusion model checkpoint, diffusion models are used to denoise latents.
output_tooltips: The model used for denoising latents.

The VAE model used for encoding and decoding images to and from latent space.

invert_output.tooltip: Invert both image and mask output

unload_model.tooltip: Unload model from VRAM after execution

background.tooltip: Choose background type: Alpha (transparent) or Color (custom background color).

image_target.tooltip: Image(s) to apply the color transform to.

image_ref.tooltip: Reference image(s) to match colors to.

source_stats.tooltip: per_frame: each frame matched to image_ref individually. uniform: pool stats across all source frames as baseline, match to image_ref. target_frame: use one chosen frame as the baseline for the transform to image_ref, applied uniformly to all frames (preserves relative differences)

target_index.tooltip: Frame index used as the source baseline for computing the transform to image_ref

ColorTransfer.name: ColorTransfer
ColorTransfer.description: Match the colors of one image to another using various algorithms.

videos.tooltip: Video segments to concatenate in input order.

codec.tooltip: Codec used to encode videos tensors. Auto uses H.264; already encoded videos remain unchanged.

complete_audio.tooltip: Optional complete soundtrack for the concatenated video. Overrides audio carried by the input videos.

output_tooltips: The concatenated video.
ConcatenateVideo.name: ConcatenateVideo
ConcatenateVideo.description: Concatenates videos in order without decoding compatible encoded inputs.

mode.tooltip: How to define the camera: orbit angles, an explicit position, or a position + quaternion.

position_x.tooltip: Camera position in world space (right-handed, Y-up).
Camera position in world space (right-handed, Y-up).

quat_w.tooltip: Camera world-rotation quaternion (three.js: looks down local -Z). Normalized for you.

target_x.tooltip: Look-at point (orbit pivot / aim). In orbit mode, move it to pan/translate the whole camera. Ignored in quaternion mode. Defaults to the origin.

roll.tooltip: Camera roll about the view axis, degrees.

fov.tooltip: Vertical field of view in degrees.

zoom.tooltip: Digital zoom (focal-length multiplier). >1 zooms in without moving the camera.

camera_type.tooltip: Projection used by Render Splat: perspective (foreshortening) or orthographic (parallel).

CreateCameraInfo.name: CreateCameraInfo
CreateCameraInfo.description: Build a camera_info. Mode 'orbit' aims with yaw/pitch/distance around the target; 'look_at' places the camera at world position. Coordinates are the viewer's world space (right-handed,Y-up).

images.tooltip: The images to create a video from.

audio.tooltip: The audio to add to the video.

bit_depth.tooltip: Auto uses 8-bit for sRGB and 10-bit for HDR. Explicit 8-bit and 10-bit choices are independent of colorspace.

color_space.tooltip: Colorspace of the input images. HDR selects BT.2020/HLG and HDR PQ selects BT.2020/PQ.

codec.tooltip: Optionally encode the video immediately. None keeps the images in tensor form; Auto uses H.264.

resolution.tooltip:
Resolution the model runs at (longest side, multiple of 14).
Lower = faster / less VRAM.
Higher = more detail.
Output is upsampled back to the original size.

resize_method.tooltip:
upper_bound_resize: scale so the longest side = resolution (caps memory, default).
lower_bound_resize: scale so the shortest side = resolution (preserves more detail on tall/wide images, uses more memory).

mode.tooltip:
mono: single view image (works with any model variant).
multiview: all images processed together for geometric consistency + camera pose (for Small/Base models only).

ref_view_strategy.tooltip:
Which view acts as the geometric anchor.
- saddle_balanced: the view most 'average' across all others (best general choice).
- saddle_sim_range: the view most visually distinct from the others.
- first / middle: fixed positional picks.

pose_method.tooltip:
How the camera field-of-view is estimated (for Small/Base models only).
- cam_dec: learned from image features.
- ray_pose: derived geometrically from the model's 3D ray output.
Affects perspective correctness of the 3D output. Try both if results look distorted.

output_tooltips:
Dictionary of non-normalized tensors.
Always has the keys: depth, image, mode.
Optional keys: sky (for Mono/Metric), confidence (for Small/Base), extrinsics + intrinsics (for multi-view).
DA3Inference.name: DA3Inference
DA3Inference.description: Run Depth Anything 3 on an image. In multi-view mode each image is treated as a separate view of the same scene.

output.tooltip:
- depth: normalised greyscale depth image.
- depth_colored: depth mapped through the Turbo colormap.
- sky_mask: sky probability in [0, 1] (for Mono/Metric models only).
- confidence: normalised depth confidence (for Small/Base models only).

normalization.tooltip:
- v2_style: mean/std normalisation for perceptually balanced results (default).
- min_max: stretches the full depth range to [0, 1] for maximum contrast.
- raw: no scaling,preserves metric units for Metric model.

apply_sky_clip.tooltip: Clip sky-region depth to the 99th percentile of foreground depth before normalisation. Requires a sky key in the da3_geometry input (for Mono/Metric models only).

normalization.tooltip:
- v2_style: mean/std normalisation for perceptually balanced results (default).
- min_max: stretches the full depth range to [0, 1] for maximum contrast.
- raw: no scaling,preserves metric units for Metric model.

apply_sky_clip.tooltip: Clip sky-region depth to the 99th percentile of foreground depth before normalisation. Requires a sky key in the da3_geometry input (for Mono/Metric models only).

colored.tooltip: Apply the Turbo colormap to the sky mask.
Apply the Turbo colormap to the confidence map.

DA3Render.name: DA3Render
DA3Render.description: Render a depth map, confidence map, or sky mask from Depth Anything 3 geometry data.

load_device.tooltip: Initial device to load the model to, NOT recommended with the larger models unless you have 48GB+ VRAM

channels.tooltip: Number of audio channels (1 for mono, 2 for stereo).

The number of latent images in the batch.

height.tooltip: The height of the latent images in pixels.

accumulate.tooltip: Return output_value from every iteration when enabled; otherwise return only the final iteration.

output_value.tooltip: Value returned by End Loop. It returns the final iteration or all iterations according to accumulate.

next_iteration_value.tooltip: Value sent from End Loop back to Start Loop for the next iteration.

terminations.tooltip: Connect outputs that must execute on every iteration. Their values are not returned.

termination.tooltip: Connect a preview or side-effect output that must execute on every iteration. Its value is not returned.

FluxKontextImageScale.description: This node resizes the image to one that is more optimal for flux kontext.

model_name.tooltip: Select a frame interpolation model to load. Models must be placed in the 'frame_interpolation' folder.

GetImageRangeFromBatch.name: GetImageRangeFromBatch

GetImageRangeFromBatch.description: Returns a range of images from a batch.

GetImageSize.name: GetImageSize

GetImageSizeAndCount.name: GetImageSizeAndCount
GetImageSizeAndCount.description:
Returns width, height and batch size of the image,  
and passes it through unchanged.

video.tooltip: The video to extract components from.

GetVideoComponents.name: GetVideoComponents
GetVideoComponents.description: Extracts video frames, audio, frame rate, bit depth, and color space.

GrowMaskWithBlur.name: GrowMaskWithBlur
GrowMaskWithBlur.description:
# GrowMaskWithBlur
- mask: Input mask or mask batch
- expand: Expand or contract mask or mask batch by a given amount
- incremental_expandrate: increase expand rate by a given amount per frame
- tapered_corners: use tapered corners
- flip_input: flip input mask
- blur_radius: value higher than 0 will blur the mask
- lerp_alpha: alpha value for interpolation between frames
- decay_factor: decay value for interpolation between frames
- fill_holes: fill holes in the mask (slow)

frame_rate.tooltip: The framerate of the input image sequence

duration.tooltip: Duration of the audio to generate in seconds

prompt.default: A person walks on frozen ice

sampler.tooltip: These were included with the official repo, but only Euler seems decent...

batch_size.tooltip: Number of audio variations to generate at once

force_offload.tooltip: Offload models from VRAM after generation

torch_compile_cfg.tooltip: Compile the model blocks with this configuration (applied lazily before denoising).

block_swap_args.tooltip: Enable BlockSwap VRAM optimization during sampling.

precision.tooltip: Compute dtype for non-quantized params and autocast (auto = detect from checkpoint)

quantization.tooltip: FP8 weight-only storage for Linear layers, saves a few GB VRAM (compute still fp16/bf16)

overlap.tooltip: Number of overlapping frames between source and new images

overlap_mode.tooltip: Method to use for overlapping frames

new_images.tooltip: The new images to extend with

ImageBatchExtendWithOverlap.description:

First input source and overlap amount to get the starting frames for the extension.

output_tooltips: The original source images (passthrough)
The input images used as the starting point for extension
The extended images with overlap, if no new images are provided this will be empty

pad_factor.tooltip: Extra margin around the mask bounding box as a multiplier.

grow_mask.tooltip: Grow or shrink the mask by this many pixels before cropping.

background.tooltip: Background color behind the masked subject.

columns.tooltip: The number of columns in the grid.

rows.tooltip: The number of rows in the grid. Set to 0 for automatic calculation.

ImageGridtoBatch.name: ImageGridtoBatch
ImageGridtoBatch.description: Converts a grid of images to a batch of images.

ImageResizeKJv2.name: ImageResizeKJv2
ImageResizeKJv2.description:
Resizes the image to the specified width and height.  
Size can be retrieved from the input.

Keep proportions keeps the aspect ratio of the image, by  
highest dimension.

algorithm.tooltip: Lottes-style rational expansion blended with a calibrated monotonic log-gain curve.

target_luminance.tooltip: Peak-white target in nits. 0 keeps the calibrated rendering. Dark images are not normalized to this peak.

ImageSDRToHDR.name: ImageSDRToHDR
ImageSDRToHDR.description: Expand sRGB brightness into Rec.2020 HLG HDR. Save the result with the HDR color space selected. Alpha is preserved.

ImageStitch.name: ImageStitch
ImageStitch.description:
Stitches image2 to image1 in the specified direction.
If image2 is not provided, returns image1 unchanged.
Optional spacing can be added between images.

noise_mask.tooltip: Add a noise mask to the latent so sampling will only happen within the mask. Might improve results or completely break things depending on the model.

model.tooltip: The model used for denoising the input latent.

seed.tooltip: The random seed used for creating the noise.

steps.tooltip: The number of steps used in the denoising process.

cfg.tooltip: The Classifier-Free Guidance scale balances creativity and adherence to the prompt. Higher values result in images more closely matching the prompt however too high values will negatively impact quality.

sampler_name.tooltip: The algorithm used when sampling, this can affect the quality, speed, and style of the generated output.

scheduler.tooltip: The scheduler controls how noise is gradually removed to form the image.

positive.tooltip: The conditioning describing the attributes you want to include in the image.

negative.tooltip: The conditioning describing the attributes you want to exclude from the image.

denoise.tooltip: The amount of denoising applied, lower values will maintain the structure of the initial image allowing for image to image sampling.

KSampler.name: KSampler
KSampler.description: Uses the provided model, positive and negative conditioning to denoise the latent image.
output_tooltips: The denoised latent.

img_compression.tooltip: Amount of compression to apply on image.

force_offload.tooltip: If true, the model will be offloaded to the offload device

crease_angle.tooltip: Edges whose dihedral angle exceeds this value (degrees) stay hard (vertices are split). 180 = fully smooth; lower preserves sharp edges (e.g. ~30-60 for hard-surface).

MeshSmoothNormals.name: MeshSmoothNormals
MeshSmoothNormals.description: Compute smooth per-vertex normals and attach them to the mesh. Meshes without normals are shaded flat (per-face) by glTF viewers; this makes them shade smoothly. With crease_angle below 180, edges sharper than the threshold are kept hard by splitting vertices along them.

MeshToFile3D.name: MeshToFile3D
MeshToFile3D.description: Serialize a mesh to a GLB File3D object for Save / Preview 3D nodes, carrying its UVs, colors, normals, texture, normal/occlusion/emissive maps and material. Supports one item per batch only.

fov_x_degrees.tooltip: Horizontal field of view of the source camera. Sets the focal length used to unproject the depth map into 3D. 0 = auto-recover from the predicted points.

batch_size.tooltip: Images per inference call. Lower if you OOM on a long video / image set.

apply_mask.tooltip: Set masked-out (sky / invalid) pixels to inf in points and depth so meshing culls them. Disable to keep the raw predicted geometry everywhere; the mask is still returned separately.

refine_steps.tooltip: MoGe-3 only: sparse volumetric refinement passes over the predicted depth. More passes sharpen fine detail and edges at a roughly linear cost. 0 disables refinement. Ignored by MoGe-1 / MoGe-2.

MoGeInference.name: MoGeInference
MoGeInference.description: Run MoGe on a single image to estimate depth and geometry.

batch_index.tooltip: Which image of a batched MoGe geometry to mesh. Per-image vertex counts differ, so batches can't be stacked into a single MESH.

discontinuity_threshold.tooltip: Drop pixels whose 3x3 depth span exceeds this fraction. 0 = off.

texture.tooltip: Carry the source image through as the baseColor texture.

MoGePointMapToMesh.name: MoGePointMapToMesh
MoGePointMapToMesh.display_name: Convert MoGe Point Map to Mesh
MoGePointMapToMesh.description: Convert a MoGe point map into a 3D mesh.

output.tooltip: DirectX vs OpenGL controls the normal-map green-channel convention. DirectX: green = -Y down (Unreal). OpenGL: green = +Y up (Blender, Substance, Unity, glTF).

MoGeRender.name: MoGeRender
MoGeRender.description: Render a depth map or normal map from geometry data

model.tooltip: These models are loaded from the 'ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models' -folder

normalize_loudness.tooltip: Normalize the audio loudness to -23 LUFS

num_frames.tooltip: The total frame count to generate.

audio_cfg_scale.tooltip: When not 1.0, an extra model pass without audio conditioning is done: slower inference but more motion is allowed

multi_audio_type.tooltip: 'para' overlay speakers in parallel, 'add' concatenate sequentially

ref_target_masks.tooltip: Per-speaker semantic mask(s) in pixel space. Supply one mask per speaker (plus optional background) to guide mouth assignment

add_noise_floor.tooltip: Add a low-level noise floor to the audio to reduce silent gaps

smooth_transients.tooltip: Apply a low-pass filter to the audio to smooth out transients

model_name.tooltip: Optical flow model to load.  Files must be placed in the 'optical_flow' folder.  Today only torchvision's raft_large.pth is supported.

PreviewAny.name: PreviewAny
PreviewAny.description: Preview any input value as text.

QuadrupleCLIPLoader.description:

torch_compile.tooltip: Compile the model with torch.compile() for 10-30% faster inference after the first (warm-up) run. Requires PyTorch 2.0+.

batch_size.tooltip: Number of interpolation tasks per GPU call. Higher values improve throughput but use more VRAM. Set to 1 for the most conservative behaviour.

image.tooltip: Input image to be processed for background removal.

model.tooltip: Select the background removal model to use (RMBG-2.0, INSPYRENET, BEN).

sensitivity.tooltip: Adjust the strength of mask detection (higher values result in more aggressive detection).

process_res.tooltip: Set the processing resolution (higher values require more VRAM and may increase processing time).

mask_blur.tooltip: Specify the amount of blur to apply to the mask edges (0 for no blur, higher values for more blur).

mask_offset.tooltip: Adjust the mask boundary (positive values expand the mask, negative values shrink it).

invert_output.tooltip: Enable to invert both the image and mask output (useful for certain effects).

refine_foreground.tooltip: Use Fast Foreground Colour Estimation to optimize transparent background

unload_model.tooltip: Unload model from VRAM after execution to free up memory.

background.tooltip: Choose output type: Alpha (transparent) or Color (custom background color).

background_color.tooltip: Pick background color (supports alpha, use color picker).

ReferenceLatent.name: ReferenceLatent
ReferenceLatent.description: This node sets the guiding latent for an edit model. If the model supports it you can chain multiple to set multiple reference images.

resolution.tooltip: Voxel grid resolution (output density). 256 ~ 100k faces, 512 ~ 1M. For an exact face count, follow with Decimate Mesh.

sign_mode.tooltip: udf: robust to messy/non-manifold input. sdf: clean single surface with QEF (Quadratic Error Function) sharp-feature recovery, but needs consistent winding.

qef.tooltip: QEF (Quadratic Error Function) dual-vertex placement for sharper edges.

drop_inverted_components.tooltip: Drop inward-normal (negative-volume) closed components — the UDF inner shell.

drop_enclosed_components.tooltip: Drop components inside the largest's bbox that fail a point-in-mesh raycast. Disable for legitimate nested parts.

qef.tooltip: QEF (Quadratic Error Function) dual-vertex placement (recovers sharp features) vs edge-crossing centroid.

manifold.tooltip: Manifold Dual Contouring: 1-4 dual verts/voxel for multi-sheet cases. Slower.

band.tooltip: Narrow-band width in voxel units. In UDF mode also offsets the surface.

project_back.tooltip: Linearly interpolate vertices toward the original surface (0 = pure DC, 1 = snapped).

fix_poles.tooltip: Collapse valence-3 vertex pairs (DC T-junction artifact).

smooth_iters.tooltip: Taubin smoothing iterations (0 = off). 2-3 cleans DC staircase-like artifacts; higher over-smooth QEF edges.

drop_small_components.tooltip: Drop components below this fraction of the largest's face count. 0 disables.

precluster_max_verts.tooltip: Cap input vertex count before the field queries, inputs above this are cluster-decimated to it first. Prevents OOM on huge meshes.

RemeshMesh.name: RemeshMesh
RemeshMesh.description: Re-extracts a uniformly tessellated mesh via a narrow-band distance field + Dual Contouring, on the active compute device. Normalizes messy / non-manifold / self-intersecting topology; run before Decimate Mesh to hit an exact face count. Output stays welded.

bg_removal_model.tooltip: Background removal model used to generate the mask

image.tooltip: Input image to remove the background from

output_tooltips: Generated foreground mask
RemoveBackground.name: RemoveBackground
RemoveBackground.description: Generates a foreground mask to remove the background from an image using a background removal model.

mode.tooltip: What to render. auto: texture if present, else vertex colours, else shaded clay.

model_3d_info.tooltip: Model transform from the same Load3D / Preview3D viewer. Connect it with camera_info to match the viewer framing.

VHS_BatchManager.name: VHS_BatchManager
VHS_BatchManager.description:
Meta Batch Manager 🎥🅥🅗🅢
Split the processing of a very long video into sets of smaller Meta Batches
The Meta Batch Manager allows for extremely long input videos to be processed when all other methods for fitting the content in RAM fail. It does not effect VRAM usage.
It must be connected to at least one Input (a Load Video or Load Images) AND at least one Video Combine
It functions by holding both the inputs and ouputs open between executions, and automatically requeue's the workflow until one of the inputs is unable to provide additional images.
Because each sub execution only contains a subset of the total frames, each sub execution creates a hard window which temporal smoothing can not be applied across. This results in jumps in the output.
[-]
Outputs:
[-]
meta_batch: Add all connected nodes to this Meta Batch
[-]
Widgets:
[-]
frames_per_batch: How many frames to process for each sub execution. If loading as image, each frame will use about 50MB of RAM (not VRAM), and this can safely be set in the 100-1000 range, depending on available memory. When loading and combining from latent space (no blue image noodles exist), this value can be much higher, around the 2,000 to 20,000 range

VHS_LoadAudioUpload.name: VHS_LoadAudioUpload
VHS_LoadAudioUpload.description:
Load Audio (Upload) 🎥🅥🅗🅢
Loads an audio file from the input directory
Very similar in functionality to the built-in LoadAudio. It was originally added before VHS swapped to use Comfy's internal AUDIO format, but provides the additional options for start time and duration
[-]
Outputs:
[-]
audio: The loaded audio
[-]
Widgets:
[-]
audio: The audio file to be loaded.
[-]
start_time: An offset from the start of the sound file that the audio should start from
[-]
duration: A maximum limit for the audio. Disabled if 0
[-]
choose audio to upload: An upload button is provided to upload an audio file to the input folder

VHS_LoadVideo.name: VHS_LoadVideo
VHS_LoadVideo.description:
Load Video 🎥🅥🅗🅢
Loads a video from the input folder
[-]
Inputs:
[-]
meta_batch: (optional) Connect to a Meta Batch manager to divide extremely long sequences into sub batches. See the documentation for Meta Batch Manager
[-]
vae: (optional) If provided the node will output latents instead of images. This drastically reduces the required RAM (not VRAM) when working with long (100+ frames) sequences
Using this is strongly encouraged unless connecting to a node that requires a blue image connection such as Apply Controllnet
[-]
Outputs:
[-]
IMAGE: The loaded images
[-]
frame_count: The length of images just returned
[-]
audio: The audio from the loaded video
[-]
video_info: Exposes additional info about the video such as the source frame rate, or the total length
[-]
LATENT: The loaded images pre-converted to latents. Only available when a vae is connected
[-]
Widgets:
[-]
video: The video file to be loaded. Lists all files with a video extension in the ComfyUI/Input folder
[-]
force_rate: Drops or duplicates frames so that the produced output has the target frame rate. Many motion models are trained on videos of a specific frame rate and will give better results if input matches that frame rate. If set to 0, all frames are returned. May give unusual results with inputs that have a variable frame rate like animated gifs. Reducing this value can also greatly reduce the execution time and memory requirements.
[-]
force_size: Previously was used to provide suggested resolutions. Instead, custom_width and custom_height can be disabled by setting to 0.
[-]
custom_width: Allows for an arbitrary width to be entered, cropping to maintain aspect ratio if both are set
[-]
custom_height: Allows for an arbitrary height to be entered, cropping to maintain aspect ratio if both are set
[-]
frame_load_cap: The maximum number of frames to load. If 0, all frames are loaded.
[-]
skip_first_frames: A number of frames which are discarded before producing output.
[-]
select_every_nth: Similar to frame rate. Keeps only the first of every n frames and discard the rest. Has better compatibility with variable frame rate inputs such as gifs. When combined with force_rate, select_every_nth_applies after force_rate so the resulting output has a frame rate equivalent to force_rate/select_every_nth. select_every_nth does not apply to skip_first_frames
[-]
format: Updates other widgets so that only values supported by the given format can be entered and provides recommended defaults.
[-]
choose video to upload: An upload button is provided to upload local files to the input folder
[-]
videopreview: Displays a preview for the selected video input. If advanced previews is enabled, this preview will reflect the frame_load_cap, force_rate, skip_first_frames, and select_every_nth values chosen. If the video has audio, it will also be previewed when moused over. Additional preview options can be accessed with right click.

VHS_SelectEveryNthImage.name: VHS_SelectEveryNthImage
VHS_SelectEveryNthImage.description:
Select Every Nth Image 🎥🅥🅗🅢
Keep only 1 image for every interval
[-]
Inputs:
[-]
images: The input image
[-]
Outputs:
[-]
IMAGE: The output images
[-]
count: The number of images in the input
[-]
Widgets:
[-]
select_every_nth: The interval from which one frame is kept. 1 means no frames are skipped.
[-]
skip_first_images: A number of frames which that is skipped from the start. This applies before select_every_nth. As a result, multiple copies of the node can each have a different skip_first_frames to divide the image into groups

VHS_VideoCombine.name: VHS_VideoCombine
VHS_VideoCombine.description:
Video Combine 🎥🅥🅗🅢
Combine an image sequence into a video
[-]
Inputs:
[-]
images: The images to be turned into a video
[-]
audio: (optional) audio to add to the video
[-]
meta_batch: (optional) Connect to a Meta Batch manager to divide extremely long image sequences into sub batches. See the documentation for Meta Batch Manager
[-]
vae: (optional) If provided, the node will take latents as input instead of images. This drastically reduces the required RAM (not VRAM) when working with long (100+ frames) sequences
Unlike on Load Video, this isn't always a strict upgrade over using a standalone VAE Decode.
If you have multiple Video Combine outputs, then the VAE decode will be performed for each output node increasing execution time
If you make any change to output settings on the Video Combine (such as changing the output format), the VAE decode will be performed again as the decoded result is (by design) not cached
[-]
Widgets:
[-]
frame_rate: The frame rate which will be used for the output video. Consider converting this to an input and connecting this to a Load Video with Video Info(Loaded)->fps. When including audio, failure to properly set this will result in audio desync
[-]
loop_count: The number of additional times the video should repeat. Can cause performance issues when used with long (100+ frames) sequences
[-]
filename_prefix: A prefix to add to the name of the output filename. This can include subfolders or format strings.
[-]
format: The output format to use. Formats starting with, 'image' are saved with PIL, but formats starting with 'video' utilize the video_formats system. 'video' options require ffmpeg and selecting one frequently adds additional options to the node.
[-]
pingpong: Play the video normally, then repeat the video in reverse so that it 'pingpongs' back and forth. This is frequently used to minimize the appearance of skips on very short animations.
[-]
save_output: Specifies if output files should be saved to the output folder, or the temporary output folder
[-]
videopreview: Displays a preview for the processed result. If advanced previews is enabled, the output is always converted to a format viewable from the browser. If the video has audio, it will also be previewed when moused over. Additional preview options can be accessed with right click.
[-]
Common Format Widgets:
[-]
crf: Determines how much to prioritize quality over filesize. Numbers vary between formats, but on each format that includes it, the default value provides visually loss less output
[-]
pix_fmt: The pixel format to use for output. Alternative options will often have higher quality at the cost of increased file size and reduced compatibility with external software.
[-]
yuv420p: The most common and default format
[-]
yuv420p10le: Use 10 bit color depth. This can improve color quality when combined with 16bit input color depth
[-]
yuva420p: Include transparency in the output video
[-]
input_color_depth: VHS supports outputting 16bit images. While this produces higher quality output, the difference usually isn't visible without postprocessing and it significantly increases file size and processing time.
[-]
save_metadata: Determines if metadata for the workflow should be included in the output video file

VideoDepthAnythingOutput.display_name: Video Depth Anything Output Depth Map

VoxelToMesh.name: VoxelToMesh
VoxelToMesh.description: Converts a voxel grid to a mesh.

device.tooltip: Where to keep the cache. cpu (RAM) is the safe choice, the cache will not fit in VRAM alongside the model at typical sizes. gpu (VRAM) can be faster if it fits.

dtype.tooltip: Storage precision. default stores the activations in the model's compute dtype. int8 halves the cache, int4 quarters it, convrot is used to retain accuracy.

WanAnimate2Cache.name: WanAnimate2Cache
WanAnimate2Cache.description: Caches the pose-video's per-block activations so it runs once instead of on every sampling step. Roughly halves generation time Tradeoff is ~12.5 GB of system RAM at 480x832/81 frames in bf16 (scales with resolution and length). With context windows each window is cached separately, so RAM scales with the window count; use the static_standard schedule, as uniform schedules shift the windows every step and nothing ever recurs to hit the cache.

batch_size.tooltip: Number of videos to generate simultaneously.

video_frame_offset.tooltip: Frames to seek into the pose video. Connect to the video_frame_offset output of the previous node when extending.

pose_strength.tooltip: Scales the pose video's influence on the motion. 1.0 is the trained behavior; below weakens adherence, above amplifies. 0.0 mutes it but does not fully remove it.

pose_start_percent.tooltip: Sampling percent at which the pose influence starts. Outside the window the pose branch is skipped entirely, which also speeds those steps up.

pose_end_percent.tooltip: Sampling percent at which the pose influence ends. Motion is mostly established early, so e.g. 0.7 can loosen fine detail while keeping the choreography.

reference_image_strength.tooltip: Scales how strongly generated frames attend to the reference image's latent frame. Below 1.0 loosens identity/appearance adherence (e.g. to let the prompt restyle), above tightens it against drift.

pose_video.tooltip: The video whose motion is transferred to the reference character.

clip_vision_output.tooltip: CLIP vision of the reference image.

positive_pose.tooltip: Prompt for the pose-video branch, describing the motion rather than the character. Defaults to positive. Used for both the cond and uncond passes.

clip_vision_output_pose.tooltip: CLIP vision of the pose video's first frame. Defaults to clip_vision_output.

continue_motion.tooltip: Previous motion sequence to continue from for temporal consistency.

output_tooltips: Number of latent frames that should be trimmed before decoding.
Number of overlapping image frames when extending a video.
Frames to seek into the pose video.
WanAnimate2ToVideo.name: WanAnimate2ToVideo
WanAnimate2ToVideo.description: Animate a character in a reference image using a video, effectively replicating the facial animation, body motion and hands gesture from the video.

ref_pad_image.tooltip: Fills the padding frames of the image conditioning with this image instead of gray, anchoring identity without pinning frames (SVI-style anti-drift padding, used by models such as ID-V2V).

mask_1.tooltip: Mask for the first speaker, required if using two audio inputs.

mask_2.tooltip: Mask for the second speaker, required if using two audio inputs.

motion_frame_count.tooltip: Number of previous frames to use as motion context.

blocks_to_swap.tooltip: Number of transformer blocks to swap, the 14B model has 40, while the 1.3B and 5B models have 30 blocks. LongCat-video has 48

use_non_blocking.tooltip: Use non-blocking memory transfer for offloading, reserves more RAM but is faster

vace_blocks_to_swap.tooltip: Number of VACE blocks to swap, the VACE model has 15 blocks

prefetch_blocks.tooltip: Number of blocks to prefetch ahead, can speed up processing but increases memory usage. 1 is usually enough to offset speed loss from block swapping, use the debug option to confirm it for your system

block_swap_debug.tooltip: Enable debug logging for block swapping

WanVideoBlockSwap.name: WanVideoBlockSwap
WanVideoBlockSwap.description: Settings for block swapping, reduces VRAM use by swapping blocks to CPU memory

combine_embeds.tooltip: Method to combine multiple clip embeds

tiles.tooltip: Use matteo's tiled image encoding for improved accuracy

enable_vae_tiling.tooltip: Drastically reduces memory use but will introduce seams at tile stride boundaries. The location and number of seams is dictated by the tile stride size. The visibility of seams can be controlled by increasing the tile size. Seams become less obvious at 1.5x stride and are barely noticeable at 2x stride size. Which is to say if you use a stride width of 160, the seams are barely noticeable with a tile width of 320.

tile_x.tooltip: Tile width in pixels. Smaller values use less VRAM but will make seams more obvious.

tile_y.tooltip: Tile height in pixels. Smaller values use less VRAM but will make seams more obvious.

tile_stride_x.tooltip: Tile stride width in pixels. Smaller values use less VRAM but will introduce more seams.

tile_stride_y.tooltip: Tile stride height in pixels. Smaller values use less VRAM but will introduce more seams.

enable_vae_tiling.tooltip: Drastically reduces memory use but may introduce seams

tile_x.tooltip: Tile size in pixels, smaller values use less VRAM, may introduce more seams

tile_y.tooltip: Tile size in pixels, smaller values use less VRAM, may introduce more seams

tile_stride_x.tooltip: Tile stride in pixels, smaller values use less VRAM, may introduce more seams

tile_stride_y.tooltip: Tile stride in pixels, smaller values use less VRAM, may introduce more seams

noise_aug_strength.tooltip: Strength of noise augmentation, helpful for leapfusion I2V where some noise can add motion and give sharper results

latent_strength.tooltip: Additional latent multiplier, helpful for leapfusion I2V where lower values allow for more motion

frame_window_size.tooltip: The number of frames to process at once, should be a value the model is generally good at.

motion_frame.tooltip: Driven frame length used in the long video generation. Basically the overlap length.

force_offload.tooltip: Whether to force offload the model within the loop for VAE operations, enable if you encounter memory issues.

colormatch.tooltip: Color matching method to use between the windows

tiled_vae.tooltip: Use tiled VAE encoding for reduced memory use

mode.tooltip: The sampling strategy to use in the long video generation loop, should match the model used

output_path.tooltip: If set, will save each window's resulting frames to this folder, also DISABLES returning the final video tensor to save memory

WanVideoImageToVideoMultiTalk.name: WanVideoImageToVideoMultiTalk
WanVideoImageToVideoMultiTalk.description: Enables Multi/InfiniteTalk long video generation sampling method, the video is created in windows with overlapping frames. Not compatible or necessary to be used with context windows and many other features besides Multi/InfiniteTalk.

lora.tooltip: LORA models are expected to be in ComfyUI/models/loras with .safetensors extension

strength.tooltip: LORA strength, set to 0.0 to unmerge the LORA

low_mem_load.tooltip: Load the LORA model with less VRAM usage, slower loading. This affects ALL LoRAs, not just the current one. No effect if merge_loras is False

merge_loras.tooltip: Merge LoRAs into the model, otherwise they are loaded on the fly. Always disabled for GGUF and scaled fp8 models. This affects ALL LoRAs, not just the current one

WanVideoLoraSelect.name: WanVideoLoraSelect
WanVideoLoraSelect.description: Select a LoRA model from ComfyUI/models/loras

model.tooltip: These models are loaded from the 'ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models' -folder

quantization.tooltip: Optional quantization method, 'disabled' acts as autoselect based by weights. Scaled modes only work with matching weights, _fast modes (fp8 matmul) require CUDA compute capability >= 8.9 (NVIDIA 4000 series and up), e4m3fn generally can not be torch.compiled on compute capability < 8.9 (3000 series and under)

load_device.tooltip: Initial device to load the model to, NOT recommended with the larger models unless you have 48GB+ VRAM

vram_management_args.tooltip: Alternative offloading method from DiffSynth-Studio, more aggressive in reducing memory use than block swapping, but can be slower

extra_model.tooltip: Extra model to add to the main model, ie. VACE or MTV Crafter

rms_norm_function.tooltip: RMSNorm function to use, 'pytorch' is the new native torch RMSNorm, which is faster (when not using torch.compile mostly) but changes results slightly. 'default' is the original WanRMSNorm

WanVideoPassImagesFromSamples.name: WanVideoPassImagesFromSamples
WanVideoPassImagesFromSamples.description: Gets possible already decoded images from the samples dictionary, used with Multi/InfiniteTalk sampling
output_tooltips: Decoded images from the samples dictionary
Output path if provided in the samples dictionary

force_offload.tooltip: Moves the model to the offload device after sampling

riflex_freq_index.tooltip: Frequency index for RIFLEX, disabled when 0, default 6. Allows for new frames to be generated after without looping

samples.tooltip: init Latents to use for video2video process

batched_cfg.tooltip: Batch cond and uncond for faster sampling, possibly faster on some hardware, uses more memory

rope_function.tooltip: Comfy's RoPE implementation doesn't use complex numbers and can thus be compiled, that should be a lot faster when using torch.compile. Chunked version has reduced peak VRAM usage when not using torch.compile

start_step.tooltip: Start step for the sampling, 0 means full sampling, otherwise samples only from this step

end_step.tooltip: End step for the sampling, -1 means full sampling, otherwise samples only until this step

add_noise_to_samples.tooltip: Add noise to the samples before sampling, needed for video2video sampling when starting from clean video

use_disk_cache.tooltip: Cache the text embeddings to disk for faster re-use, under the custom_nodes/ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper/text_embed_cache directory

device.tooltip: Device to run the text encoding on.

extender_args.tooltip: Use this node to extend the prompt with additional text.

WanVideoTextEncodeCached.name: WanVideoTextEncodeCached
WanVideoTextEncodeCached.description:
Encodes text prompts into text embeddings. This node loads and completely unloads the T5 after done,  
leaving no VRAM or RAM imprint. If prompts have been cached before T5 is not loaded at all.  
negative output is meant to be used with NAG, it contains only negative prompt embeddings.  

Additionally you can provide a Qwen LLM model to extend the positive prompt with either one  
of the original Wan templates or a custom system prompt.
output_tooltips: The text embeddings for both prompts
The text embeddings for the negative prompt only (for NAG)
Positive prompt to display prompt extender results

use_cpu_cache.tooltip: Reduces VRAM usage, but slows the VAE down a lot

verbose.tooltip: Enables memory usage logging when using the model
